soft_notes.topic: Pydantic ValidationError vs domain ValidationError naming overlap
soft_notes.where: src.domain.exceptions.ValidationError (T-003) shares the class NAME 'ValidationError' with pydantic.ValidationError
soft_notes.observation: FastAPI registers its own handler for pydantic.ValidationError that returns 422 with the standard {detail: [...]} list-of-errors body. Our handler is on the DOMAIN ValidationError class, a different Python type. They coexist correctly because @app.exception_handler dispatches on exact class identity. Logged here so future contributors don't 'fix' by renaming or merging — both paths are intentional.
soft_notes.actionable_for: Document in T-013 GradeService when domain ValidationError is raised (it's currently used for service-level validation that Pydantic missed).

soft_notes.topic: IntegrityError generic message can swallow useful 409 context
soft_notes.observation: Plan-prescribed behaviour for security (avoid leaking constraint names + SQL). Practical consequence: TC-035 and TC-038 assert that the 409 body DETAIL contains 'grade_code' / 'design_id, grade_id'. These assertions pass only when the ConflictError path runs (service pre-check), NOT when IntegrityError fires as the rare-race fallback. This is acceptable because: (a) tests run in serial, so service pre-check always wins; (b) the IntegrityError path is a production safety net only.
soft_notes.actionable_for: Sprint-close: if production observes IntegrityError-path 409s, consider parsing exc.orig.constraint_name and emitting a less leaky but more informative detail (e.g. 'duplicate grade_code'). Out of scope for S1.
